title: Decentralized Deliberation for Future Imagination & Coordination
description:
The hardest problem is not intelligence — it's coordination. As we imagine better futures, how do we navigate them together when our dreams, and our nightmares, pull in different directions?

This talk maps the deliberation and sense-making landscape and shares practical lessons from real deployments. Key insights: why classic forum-style discussions and voting-only governance can lead to low engagement and even polarization; how active listening (opinion mapping, wikisurveys) and passive listening (analyzing existing discourse with LLM sense-making) complement each other; and how to compose them into processes. This is relevant for decentralized, democratic participation across use cases from DAOs to cities and states.

I'll close with the interoperability challenge: deliberation tools today are often siloed — and share how an open standard, Decentralized Deliberation Stack, can address it, and how anyone can contribute to the neutral W3C Community Group.
